lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the effect of dilation on lines through and off the center
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: the effect of dilation on lines through and off the center

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal angles. Similar?

steps: The third angles must match too.

items.prompt: What happens to a line through the centre of dilation?

steps: Every point stays on the ray from the centre.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (4, -6) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 12 becomes a side of length 24. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 12; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 40° and ∠B = 105°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 40° and ∠E = 105°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away
is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped onto itself

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-3, -3) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 7 becomes a side of length 28. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 21; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 1/4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 4

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 68° and ∠B = 50°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 68° and ∠E = 50°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a parallel line
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped onto itself
